rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion narrow and precedent-anchored (Reno/Ashcroft strict-scrutiny tailoring and evidentiary burden) while holding only that Texas’s adult-facing verification mandate is unconstitutional on this record. Kavanaugh likely writes (or joins) a principal dissent distinguishing COPA and emphasizing privacy-preserving verification, with Thomas and/or Alito adding separate dissents grounded in Ginsberg/history and pragmatic enforcement concerns.
